title: Signal-ranking rollback advisor for canary exits
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Canary rollouts today use fixed threshold heuristics across multiple signals (latency, error rate, token cost, throughput). This causes noisy or late rollbacks when signals disagree or when traffic cohorts exhibit short spikes. Goal: build a Signal-ranking Rollback Advisor that synthesizes multiple SLO signals into a ranked list of root-cause candidates and a single actionable recommendation (recommend rollback / continue / hold) with confidence and suggested hysteresis parameters. The advisor should be usable as a dry-run analysis for PMs/engineers and as an optionally-enforced auto-rollback trigger integrated with the rollout engine. It must support cost-normalized scoring (e.g., token cost per successful request) and be traffic-aware (weight signals by cohort and request volume).
acceptance_criteria: Advisor computes a per-canary multi-signal score and ranks signals by contribution (latency, p95/p99, error rate, token cost, throughput) for a live canary
Produces a clear recommendation: rollback / continue / hold and a numeric confidence score (0-1) that maps to policy tiers
Exposes tunable hysteresis and cooldown settings to avoid flapping; settings are honored by the rollout engine in auto-rollback mode
Backtest harness runs advisor against three historical canaries (billing spike incident, model-quality regression, infra degradation) and reproduces expected decisions
API and Console surface: (a) per-canary advisor output, (b) signal contribution waterfall, (c) suggested threshold adjustments, and (d) link to replay/backtest artifacts
Unit tests for scoring logic and integration tests verifying rollout engine obeys advisor decisions under policy=auto-rollback and policy=recommend-only
Performance: advisor eval <200ms per canary decision at 1k TPS aggregation (offline/batch acceptable for heavy analytics; online decision path must meet target)
Documentation: PRD, runbook for incident handling, and short SDK example for enabling advisor in Dedicated/Private deployments

notes: Design decisions: use a lightweight probabilistic ranker rather than heavy causal inference to get explainability and fast evals in the critical path.

Scoring: each signal is transformed into a normalized z-score vs recent baseline, then multiplied by a tunable weight and traffic-volume factor. Token cost is normalized by successful-completion rate to surface costly regressions.
Hysteresis: recommend both time-based cooldown and evidence-threshold smoothing (exponential decay). Default cooldown = 10m, default smoothing alpha = 0.25.
Failure modes: advisor may overweight noisy low-volume cohorts; mitigation is min-volume gating and cohort-aware weights.
Privacy: advisor inputs include telemetry; do not send PII to advisor service; ensure compatibility with Private/VPC deployments (local telemetry hooks).

Trade-offs: conservative preset avoids customer-facing rollbacks but may delay mitigation; aggressive preset improves safety at cost of false positives. Default tuned to minimize customer-visible errors while keeping cost outliers detectable.
Related work: reuses KV-cache and batching telemetry from observability pipeline to reduce instrumentation delta. Will reuse signal extraction helpers from ENG-34120.
Success metrics: reduction in time-to-rollback for true regressions by >=30% in pilot, false-rollback rate <1% over 30 days, no degradation in normal canary completion rate.
Fallback: if advisor service fails, rollout engine reverts to legacy fixed-threshold policy and emits an alert.
Opt-in model: default mode for new canaries is recommend-only; enterprise customers can opt into auto-rollback via policy toggles.
